answer: Agents can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake in a vault before it can vote or claim rewards. A randomly sampled set of peers checks each agent’s work; if a challenge proves two identities reused the same credential or submitted fabricated evidence, the protocol burns part of their stake and caps their influence. Creating thousands of names therefore does not create free voting power: the attacker must lock real capital and risks losing it, even if activity falls to a nadir in the tundra.
